Two pages speak of one state and give it two ends. 28:51-56 says a GitHub write of yaz that fails, 'the first or a later one', is an outage: the job ends, nothing is held, the next scheduled cycle runs, decides anew from what it pulls and takes over what the failed job left. 28:58-59 keeps cek's chain-break refusal of 13 'as it is'. 13:50-52 calls a brain/integration head other than the commit the last signed state row names a chain break, a hard stop that is not repaired. The state: in a merging cycle D6 merges the candidate's pull request first and writes brain/state after it. When a request after the merge fails (the state commit's), the merge stands on brain/integration and no row names it: the test above shows it for every request after the merge (the head moved, its SHA in no ledger row, brain/state where it was, the line write_failed). The next cycle's cek then reads a head that the ledger's last naming row does not name, and loop.integration answers head_not_named (tests.test_loop_integration; cek refuses the target integration_refused before anything is decided), in every cycle after it: nothing in the loop takes the merge up, and 13 says the break is not repaired. So for the writes after the merge 28:54-55's 'the next cycle takes over what the failed job left' and 13:50-52 with 28:58-59 cannot both hold. What the build does meanwhile: exactly the above, stated as open in loop/write_cycle.py and in the test's docstring; no test holds either end as right (ledger lesson f2208). Asked of the page, one of: (a) the next cycle may take up a head that is the merge of an open decision it can prove (the head's first parent is the commit the last row names, its second parent the commit this cycle's own candidate branch gives, the pull request merged), writing the merge's rows then; (b) such a head is a chain break as 13 says and 28:54-55 is narrowed to the writes before the merge; (c) the order of D6's writes changes so that no state can stand between the two. I did not choose: (a) relaxes 13's rule for one proven shape, which is the owner's to grant (Y11), and (b) makes an outage after the merge an operator step, which L-AM1 says a failed write does not ask for.
